explanation: Track a sliding window and its largest observed character frequency. Shrink when the window length minus that frequency exceeds k. The historical maximum safely bounds the longest achievable window.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n uppercase letters.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A window can be made uniform using windowLength minus its most frequent character count replacements. The running historical maximum allows the window to grow only when an equally large feasible window has been witnessed. Shrinking on an excess requirement prevents the recorded maximum length from exceeding an achievable length; scanning every right endpoint finds an optimum.
walkthrough: For "AAABBC" with k=1, the window "AAAB" contains three As and one B, so one replacement creates four As. Extending it to "AAABB" would require two replacements. No later window is longer and feasible, so return 4.
edgeCases: k=0 reduces to the longest equal-character run.
The input alphabet is uppercase A through Z.
At most k replacements are allowed; unused replacements are permitted.
